title: Thin lines that carry meaning must reach 3:1 as rendered, not only by color
rule: When a drawing uses thin lines to convey information (metric guides, baselines, chart rules, SVG strokes), the rendered pixels must reach 3:1 against the background in every theme, not only the nominal stroke color. A 1 px stroke centred on a whole-pixel coordinate is anti-aliased over two device rows at half strength at a device pixel ratio of 1 (about 2:1 for a color that is 4.8:1 at full strength). Use a 2 px stroke or put 1 px lines on half pixels, and add a Playwright check that rasterizes the lines at the page's pixel ratio and measures the strongest pixel's contrast under both color schemes.
rationale: E11.4 (#102): the glyph compare overlay drew x-height and cap-height guides as 1 px SVG lines on integer y; the screenshots showed them at 2.06:1 light and 1.79:1 dark.
